prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Create ONE high-quality concept illustration of an EXPANDED PERSONAL MAGICAL WORKBENCH behind a gaming counter, for a top-down 2D fantasy card game. This is a close-up prop/environment design study, not a game screenshot and not a UI dashboard.
Composition: landscape 3:2, near-orthographic OVERHEAD VIEW, hand-painted 2D game illustration with delicate contours and rich tactile materials. The broad, deep, open work surface fills the lower 75–80 percent of the image and almost its full width. It must feel like a usable artisan's bench unfolded in front of the player, with generous working depth, substantial visible dark wood, beveled corners, side wings, subtle brass hinge seams and leather pads. It is NOT a narrow chest, NOT a small four-hole casket, NOT four circular dashboard gauges in a row. Do not draw an upright lid, legs, a room, or a dramatic perspective.
At the TOP 20 percent, show a shallow raised front counter with dark burgundy gaming felt and a fine antique-gold border. A low black-walnut ledge separates this far-side playing surface from the player's near-side workbench. The materials and joint make these two parts of one physical counter. Keep the entire main bench outline readable.
The TWO ACTIVE MAGICAL ARTIFACTS are the visual heroes, substantially larger and more detailed than a playing card, centered across the main working surface:
LEFT-CENTER: a large ornate shield-shaped pendant with antique gold skeleton, dark wine-red enamel, a small ivory diamond and precise engraved details; resting on a broad burgundy leather work pad with small brass retaining fingers.
RIGHT-CENTER: a tall slender faceted dark-red crystal lying FLAT in an elongated oval antique-brass cage, on its own differently shaped leather pad and low metal supports. It must read as a handheld magical artifact, not a bottle or a huge industrial machine.
The artifact silhouettes dominate. Their bases integrate restrained segmented brass arcs or short physical tick marks, some softly lit amber to indicate the current batch. Keep the brass progress accents subordinate to the actual artifacts; no enclosing giant clock dials. Warm production light is concentrated around the two active relics.
EXACTLY TWO ADDITIONAL EMPTY EQUIPMENT WORK POSITIONS are reserved nearer the foreground left and right corners. Show simple flat dark-leather pad areas with subtle mounting marks, much lower contrast than the active artifacts. These are empty future workstations on the same expansive bench, not drawers and not additional relics. The four total work positions follow a broad two-by-two arrangement with generous shared wooden working space, not a rigid paneled UI grid. No enclosing individual boxes or thick dividers.
Show the card-making relationship clearly: on the FRONT/FAR EDGE of the LEFT active workstation, just below the ledge, an ivory shield card is captured sliding across the low counter lip toward the burgundy playing surface. One card only, a fine gold frame and simple shield symbol, with a restrained warm trace connecting it to the guardian work pad. This is a transient completion moment. The output is an OPEN FLAT MANIFESTATION SURFACE, no mechanical printer slot, no conveyor, no stockpile. Do not add stored hand cards, full battle rows, extra token counters, resources, or incidental bottles/tools in this close-up.
Palette: black-brown walnut #261a15, dark burgundy #4a1724, aged antique gold #ac8c4e, a little aged ivory #e7d8b7. Warm light from upper left, readable midtones, attractive worn grain and leather, small scratches and tasteful ornament. Strongest contrast and finest detail on the active artifacts. The front felt is quieter so the workbench remains the focal point. Refined crafted fantasy, painterly not photographic, not steampunk machinery.
Minimal design annotations with thin antique-gold leader lines placed in natural margins, exactly four short Chinese labels: “前台牌面” pointing to the upper felt; “守护法器” pointing to the left active relic; “施法法器” pointing to the right active relic; “扩展工位” pointing to an empty foreground mount. No title, paragraphs, numbers, game HUD, buttons, rulers, giant arrows, watermark, human figures or hands.
The primary impression must be: the player stands behind a counter, operating a substantial personal magic workbench to create cards, then sending them forward onto the playing counter. Show this open workbench as the main subject with two beautiful working artifacts and two reserved future positions.
